verdicts.rewritten_summary: UK Foreign Office travel advisory (19 Aug 2026) warns LGBT+ travellers to Nigeria of arrest, violence, attacks, blackmail and intimidation, stating that same-sex sexual activity is illegal and can attract up to 14 years' imprisonment, and that the federal law extends to people who arrange, attend or conduct same-sex weddings and those involved with gay groups or organisations. It adds that some northern states operate Sharia law under which same-sex activity can attract the death penalty, and that breaching curfews or movement restrictions risks arrest and detention. National-framework facts the record's own summary claims for this state.

The advisory's Sharia-warning applies only to northern states, which the record notes do not cover this southern state, while the federal penalties and arrest-risk warnings apply in full.

BBC report (9 Aug 2024) on the death of Nigerian transgender TikToker 'Abuja Area Mama' (33): her beaten body was found along the Katampe–Mabushi expressway in the capital, suspected murder, roughly a year after she had said she feared for her life; an investigation was announced. The article notes that despite formal constitutional guarantees of non-discrimination and private/family life, mass arrests and detention of LGBTQ+ people are common, especially in northern states — national-climate evidence the record's summary relies on for this state.
